The `autoescape=True` kwarg is also redundant here: on the `directory=` path, Starlette's `_create_env` already does `env_options.setdefault("autoescape", True)`. The kwarg adds nothing except the deprecated passthrough. pytest has no filterwarnings=error setting, so the test suite will not catch this.

agent_notes: Escaping behavior today: with Starlette 0.52.1, autoescape stays True through both the old and the new form, so this diff causes no XSS regression right now. The template output is the same.
Unlike the prior commit message, Starlette 0.52.1 has not removed **env_options yet. It only deprecates them (templating.py:92-95). The risk lies ahead: removal would raise a TypeError at import.

Blast radius: routes.py builds `templates` at module scope. Five modules import it: triggarr/__main__.py, triggarr/search/scheduler.py, tests/test_web.py, tests/test_middleware.py and tests/test_root_path.py. A constructor failure there means the process cannot start at all, which takes down the web UI and the scheduler, not just one route.

Dependency exposure: the Docker build installs with `pip install .` from an unpinned `fastapi`, not from uv.lock. Image builds therefore follow the newest Starlette, which makes the future break likely to land in production without any code change.
No schema, migration or performance impact. Templates are built once at import.
Verdict: not blocking today, but the diff undoes a deliberate fix one commit back for no functional gain. Recommend dropping it or removing only the redundant autoescape kwarg.

Starlette's `Jinja2Templates.__init__` treats any `**env_options` (including `autoescape`) as a deprecated path: it emits `DeprecationWarning: Extra environment options are deprecated. Use a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead.` at import time, which I reproduced by running `uv run pytest` against this project's locked starlette 0.52.1.
findings.title: Jinja2Templates reverted to deprecated env_options passthrough for autoescape
findings.why_it_matters: I verified that under the project's currently locked starlette==0.52.1, `_create_env` still honors `env_options.setdefault('autoescape', True)` so Jinja2 autoescaping is NOT currently broken (full test suite passes, 466/466) — but the whole point of the original fix (per its own commit message) was that Starlette is moving this kwarg passthrough toward removal, and autoescape silently defaults to False in Jinja2 once a bare `jinja2.Environment` is built without it. If a future starlette bump drops the deprecated fallback, HTML autoescaping across every template (dashboard cards, log lines, config values) would silently stop, reopening stored-XSS surface in a dashboard that renders instance names, search logs, and config fields.

findings.fix_hint: Keep the explicit jinja2.Environment(autoescape=True) passed through env=, and verify application import against the dependencies resolved by the Docker build.
findings.problem: Starlette 1.0 removed Jinja2Templates' extra environment arguments, so passing autoescape=True raises TypeError during routes.py import, preventing application startup. The Dockerfile runs `pip install .` without uv.lock, and pyproject.toml leaves FastAPI unpinned; released FastAPI versions support Starlette 1.x. The locked local Starlette 0.52.1 still accepts this argument, masking the production failure. See [Starlette's removal notes](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/blob/main/docs/release-notes.md#100rc1-february-23-2026) and [FastAPI release notes](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes/).
